studies.Study: Wang Y et al. (2021) [PMID: 32238007] — estimate 1 · Mixed
studies.Reference: Dietary Intakes of Trace Elements and the Risk of Kidney Cancer: The Singapore Chinese Health Study.
studies.Title: Dietary Intakes of Trace Elements and the Risk of Kidney Cancer: The Singapore Chinese Health Study.
studies.Authors: Wang Y, Jafar TH, Jin A, Yuan JM, Koh WP

sample_size.excerpt: Thus, the final sample size for the current analysis was 61,321 participants.
sample_size.location: Methods, Identification of kidney cancer, paragraph 1

cases.excerpt: There were 229 incident kidney cancer cases after median follow-up of 20.1 years.

effect_size.excerpt: In the fully adjusted model, the HR of kidney cancer risk when comparing the highest versus lowest quartile of dietary zinc was 1.74 (95% CI: 1.02–2.97). Conversely, dietary intakes of copper and manganese were not associated with kidney cancer risk; the corresponding HRs were 1.10 (95% CI: 0.71–1.72; P -trend=0.65) and 1.26 (95% CI: 0.83–1.91; P -trend=0.31), respectively (Model 3; Table 2 ).

confidence_interval.excerpt: Conversely, dietary intakes of copper and manganese were not associated with kidney cancer risk; the corresponding HRs were 1.10 (95% CI: 0.71–1.72; P -trend=0.65) and 1.26 (95% CI: 0.83–1.91; P -trend=0.31), respectively (Model 3; Table 2 ).

p_value.excerpt: Conversely, dietary intakes of copper and manganese were not associated with kidney cancer risk; the corresponding HRs were 1.10 (95% CI: 0.71–1.72; P -trend=0.65) and 1.26 (95% CI: 0.83–1.91; P -trend=0.31), respectively (Model 3; Table 2 ).

comparison.excerpt: For the multivariable analyses, participants were divided in quartiles based on their intake and the lowest quartile intake served as the reference group.

design.excerpt: In this study, we examined intakes of dietary zinc, copper and manganese and their associations with incident kidney cancer in a prospective cohort study of Chinese living in Singapore.

timing.excerpt: We prospectively assessed the associations of dietary zinc and other trace elements with kidney cancer risk for the first time.

continent.excerpt: Chinese adults (27,954 men and 35,303 women) aged between 45 and 74 years old were recruited. The detailed design of the Singapore Chinese Health Study has been described previously

ethnicity.excerpt: a total of 63,257 Chinese adults (27,954 men and 35,303 women) aged between 45 and 74 years old were recruited.

exposure_measurement.excerpt: We used a semi-quantitative food frequency questionnaire (FFQ), which included 165 common food items in Singapore, to measure dietary intake at baseline interviews.
exposure_measurement.location: Methods, Assessment of exposures and covariates, paragraph 1

gender.excerpt: a total of 63,257 Chinese adults (27,954 men and 35,303 women) aged between 45 and 74 years old were recruited.

smoking_status.excerpt: Model 2: Model 1 plus additional adjustment for energy (Kcal/day), body mass index (<18.5, 18.5-<23.0, 23.0-<27.5, ≥27.5 kg/m 2 ), history of hypertension (yes, no), history of diabetes (yes, no), smoking status (never, former and current smokers), and protein intake (g/day; quartile).
